title: DoorDash launches an AI agent you can text to order food
content:
DoorDash announced on Wednesday that it’s launching a text-to-order AI agent that lets users place orders through Apple Messages. The new tool allows users to send prompts like “order my usual,” and the agent will understand that they mean their Friday night order.
DoorDash says users can also ask for a specific dish and request a local recommendation. The agent will then search local spots and suggest a cart based on the prompt, and even text photos of the food it recommends. When ordering for a group, DoorDash says the agent can handle mixed dietary preferences and different quantities in one order.
By launching an AI agent for food ordering, DoorDash is looking to gain an edge over rivals Uber Eats and Grubhub. The launch also comes amid a growing push to adopt personal AI agents that can handle tasks without requiring users to navigate apps or websites themselves.
DoorDash is opening up a waitlist for users in the U.S. to try out the new feature.
In addition to the new AI agent, DoorDash announced that it will begin testing its delivery drones with select restaurants in Northern California.

report.summary: DoorDash launched a text-to-order AI agent in Apple Messages that understands requests like “order my usual,” recommends local dishes, and handles group orders.
report.background: DoorDash’s new agent arrives as food delivery platforms compete on convenience and speed. Uber Eats and Grubhub have also experimented with AI features, while consumers are increasingly interested in personal AI agents that complete tasks without requiring app or website navigation. Apple Messages offers a familiar, low-friction interface that could make ordering feel as easy as texting a friend. DoorDash is opening a U.S. waitlist for the feature, suggesting a cautious rollout. Separately, the company is testing delivery drones with select restaurants in Northern California, signaling broader investment in automation. The move reflects a wider shift toward conversational commerce, where AI agents handle discovery, personalization, and checkout inside messaging threads.
key_points: DoorDash’s new agent lives inside Apple Messages, so users can order by texting prompts such as “order my usual” instead of browsing the app. It interprets personal history and context, turning the messaging thread into a commerce interface. The feature is initially gated by a U.S. waitlist.

Users can ask for a specific dish or a local recommendation. The agent searches nearby restaurants, suggests a cart, and can text photos of recommended food. This adds discovery and visual decision support to conversational ordering, making the agent more than a reorder shortcut.

For group orders, DoorDash says the agent can manage mixed dietary preferences and different quantities in one order. That could reduce the friction of coordinating office lunches or family meals, where one person usually has to collect everyone’s choices and manually build the cart.

The launch is a competitive move against Uber Eats and Grubhub, as delivery platforms race to lock in AI-powered convenience. DoorDash is also testing delivery drones with select restaurants in Northern California, signaling broader automation ambitions beyond chat-based ordering. Both efforts are early-stage.
report.impact: For the AI industry, DoorDash’s agent shows how food delivery could become a major testbed for agentic commerce—AI that doesn’t just recommend but completes transactions. Rivals like Uber Eats and Grubhub will likely accelerate their own conversational ordering features. Developers should watch identity, payments, inventory, and personalization APIs that connect LLM agents to real-world services. For regular users, texting to order could be faster and more accessible than app navigation, especially for reorders and group meals. But it also raises questions about accuracy, privacy, and how much order history platforms use to personalize suggestions. Adoption will depend on whether the agent reliably handles edge cases and allergens.
report.tools: To follow this space, watch DoorDash’s U.S. waitlist and its Apple Messages integration. Comparable agentic-commerce efforts include Uber Eats AI assistants, Instacart’s Ask Instacart, and OpenAI’s Operator-style agents. Developers can experiment with open-source frameworks like LangGraph, Microsoft AutoGen, Rasa, and Botpress for conversational ordering flows, plus Twilio or Apple Messages for Business for messaging channels.
